title: Give me that book! Give it to me!
subtitle: give somebody something / give something to somebody
summary: Use both give somebody something and give something to somebody, and use give it to somebody with it and them.

lesson.heading: Two possible structures
lesson.text: A hand holds out some keys and Sarah puts her hand out to take them. There are two ways to say this. After the verbs **give**, **lend**, **pass**, **send** and **show** both structures are correct.

lesson.heading: give something to somebody
rows: These are Sue's keys. Can you **give**

lesson.heading: give somebody something
rows: an email. Did you get it?
lesson.note: There is no *to* in this structure: *Give me that book*, not ~~Give to me that book~~.

lesson.heading: buy and get somebody something
lesson.text: You can also say **buy** or **get** somebody something. With *for* the thing comes first.

examples.note: = I bought some flowers for my mother.

examples.text: Can you **get me a newspaper** when you go out?

lesson.heading: Which structure with it and them?

left.label: Both are correct
left.text: With a noun (the keys, that book) you can choose.
examples: Can you give that book **to me**?

right.label: With it and them use to
right.text: We prefer give something to somebody when the thing is **it** or **them**.
examples: I gave **it to her**. (*not* I gave her it)
Here are the keys. Give **them to your father**. (*not* Give your father them)
That's my book. Can you give **it to me**?

lesson.text: Never put *to* before the person in the short structure: *I gave Sarah the keys*, not ~~I gave to Sarah the keys~~.

exercises.prompt: Mark didn't want his old books, so he gave ___ to Sarah.
exercises.explanation: books = them, so: He gave them to Sarah.

exercises.prompt: Mark gave his tennis racket to Gary. What did he do with the racket? He gave it ___.
exercises.explanation: With it we use give it to somebody.

exercises.prompt: Mark had some things he didn't want. Match each thing with the person he gave it to.
You gave Richard a tie for his birthday. Put the words in order.
exercises.explanation: give somebody something: the person comes first, with no to.

exercises.prompt: You want the salt at dinner. Ask the person next to you.
exercises.answer: Can you pass me the salt?
exercises.explanation: pass somebody something: pass me the salt.

exercises.prompt: You need an umbrella. You ask a friend: Can you ___ an umbrella?
exercises.explanation: lend somebody something: lend me an umbrella.

exercises.prompt: You want to see the letter. You ask: Can you ___ the letter?
exercises.explanation: show somebody something: show me the letter.

exercises.prompt: You want some stamps. You ask: Can you ___ some stamps?
exercises.explanation: get somebody something = get something for somebody.

options: I gave to Sarah the keys.
exercises.explanation: give somebody something has no to; give something to somebody needs it.

exercises.prompt: I'll ___ some money if you want.
exercises.explanation: lend somebody something: I'll lend you some money.

exercises.statement: I showed to the policeman my identity card.
exercises.explanation: I showed the policeman my identity card. There is no to before the person here.

exercises.prompt: This is Lisa's bag. Can you ___?
exercises.explanation: With it we prefer give it to somebody.
